title: JLPT N2 — Business & Media
description: Keigo honorifics, proposals & strategy, technology & economy vocabulary, formal grammar, and essay reading.

units.title: Keigo & Formal Communication
units.subtitle: けいご · Mastering respectful (Sonkeigo) and humble (Kenjougo) speech

lessons.title: Respectful Speech (Sonkeigo)
lessons.objective: Elevate the actions of clients, elders, and superiors.
lessons.grammarNote: Sonkeigo (いらっしゃる, おっしゃる, ご覧になる) is ONLY used for other people's actions, never your own.

example.term: 社長は会議室にいらっしゃいます。
example.transliteration: Shachou wa kaigishitsu ni irasshaimasu.
example.translation: The president is in the meeting room.

example.term: 先生がおっしゃった通りです。
example.transliteration: Sensei ga osshatta toori desu.
example.translation: It is just as the teacher said.

example.term: こちらの資料をご覧ください。
example.transliteration: Kochira no shiryou o goran kudasai.
example.translation: Please look at this document.

example.term: どうぞお召し上がりください。
example.transliteration: Douzo omeshiagari kudasai.
example.translation: Please enjoy your meal.

example.term: この仕組みをご存じですか。
example.transliteration: Kono shikumi o gozonji desu ka.
example.translation: Are you familiar with this system?

lessons.title: Humble Speech (Kenjougo)
lessons.objective: Lower your own actions politely when addressing outsiders or seniors.
lessons.grammarNote: Kenjougo (参る, 拝見する, 伺う) shows humility for your own or your in-group's actions.

example.term: メールを拝見いたしました。
example.transliteration: Meeru o haiken itashimashita.
example.translation: I have reviewed your email.

example.term: 明日そちらに伺います。
example.transliteration: Ashita sochira ni ukagaimasu.
example.translation: I will visit your office tomorrow.

example.term: ただいま参ります。
example.transliteration: Tadaima mairimasu.
example.translation: I will be right there.

example.term: お名前は存じ上げております。
example.transliteration: Onamae wa zonjiagete orimasu.
example.translation: I am acquainted with your name.

example.term: 私が対応いたします。
example.transliteration: Watashi ga taiou itashimasu.
example.translation: I will handle it.

lessons.title: Formal Business Courtesies
lessons.objective: Use polished email and client-facing expressions.
lessons.grammarNote: Memorize fixed polite chunks like 承知いたしました and 申し訳ございません for instant fluency.

items.reading: しょうちいたしました

example.term: ご依頼の件、承知いたしました。
example.transliteration: Goirai no ken, shouchi itashimashita.
example.translation: Certainly, I understand your request.

items.reading: もうしわけございません

example.term: お待たせして申し訳ございません。
example.transliteration: Omatase shite moushiwake gozaimasen.
example.translation: I sincerely apologize for the wait.

example.term: 恐れ入りますが、もう一度お願いします。
example.transliteration: Osoreirimasu ga, mou ichido onegai shimasu.
example.translation: Excuse me, could you please repeat that?

example.term: 差し支えなければご意見をお聞かせください。
example.transliteration: Sashitsukae nakereba goiken o okikase kudasai.
example.translation: If you don't mind, please share your thoughts.

items.term: 何卒よろしくお願いします
items.reading: なにとぞよろしくおねがいします

example.term: 今後とも何卒よろしくお願いします。
example.transliteration: Kongo tomo nanitozo yoroshiku onegai shimasu.
example.translation: We kindly ask for your continued support.

units.title: Proposals, Strategy & Evaluation
units.subtitle: きかくとひょうか · Running projects and evaluating outcomes

lessons.title: Planning & Proposals
lessons.objective: Pitch ideas, examine options, and launch projects.
lessons.grammarNote: Two-kanji compounds (熟語) make business and engineering discussions concise.

example.term: 改善案をチームに提案した。
example.transliteration: Kaizen-an o chiimu ni teian shita.
example.translation: I proposed an improvement plan to the team.

example.term: 導入について慎重に検討する。
example.transliteration: Dounyuu ni tsuite shinchou ni kentou suru.
example.translation: Carefully consider the adoption.

example.term: 拡張しやすい設計を目指した。
example.transliteration: Kakuchou shiyasui sekkei o mezashita.
example.translation: Aimed for an extensible architecture.

example.term: 理想の学習体験を実現する。
example.transliteration: Risou no gakushuu taiken o jitsugen suru.
example.translation: Realize the ideal learning experience.

example.term: オープンソースの方針を維持する。
example.transliteration: Oopunsoosu no houshin o iji suru.
example.translation: Maintain the open-source policy.

lessons.title: Quality & Improvement
lessons.objective: Discuss metrics, feedback, and iterative refinement.
lessons.grammarNote: Notice the root 改 (change/improve) in 改善 (kaizen) and 改良 (improvement).

example.term: 使い勝手を大幅に改善した。
example.transliteration: Tsukaigatte o oohaba ni kaizen shita.
example.translation: Significantly improved usability.

example.term: 高い評価を得ることができた。
example.transliteration: Takai hyouka o eru koto ga dekita.
example.translation: We earned high ratings.

example.term: 教材の品質を保つ仕組み。
example.transliteration: Kyouzai no hinshitsu o tamotsu shikumi.
example.translation: A system to maintain material quality.

example.term: 記憶の効率を高める復習法。
example.transliteration: Kioku no kouritsu o takameru fukushuuhou.
example.translation: A review method that boosts memory efficiency.

example.term: 日々の積み重ねが成果につながる。
example.transliteration: Hibi no tsumikasane ga seika ni tsunagaru.
example.translation: Daily accumulation leads to results.

lessons.title: Negotiation & Consensus
lessons.objective: Reach agreements and handle constraints professionally.
lessons.grammarNote: Use 調整 (coordinate) and 合意 (consensus) when aligning stakeholders.

example.term: 日程を調整してご連絡します。
example.transliteration: Nittei o chousei shite gorenraku shimasu.
example.translation: I'll coordinate the schedule and reach out.

example.term: 全員の合意を得て決定した。
example.transliteration: Zenin no goui o ete kettei shita.
example.translation: Decided after gaining everyone's consensus.

example.term: 容量の制限を意識して設計する。
example.transliteration: Youryou no seigen o ishiki shite sekkei suru.
example.translation: Design with storage limits in mind.

example.term: モバイル対応を優先しましょう。
example.transliteration: Mobairu taiou o yuusen shimashou.
example.translation: Let's prioritize mobile support.

example.term: 毎日の学習時間を確保する。
example.transliteration: Mainichi no gakushuu jikan o kakuho suru.
example.translation: Secure daily study time.

units.title: Technology, Economy & Media
units.subtitle: ぎじゅつとけいざい · Reading articles on innovation and society

lessons.title: Innovation & Adoption
lessons.objective: Follow tech news, trends, and global diffusion.
lessons.grammarNote: N2 news passages rely heavily on compounds like 普及 (widespread adoption) and 発展 (development).

example.term: スマートフォンが急速に普及した。
example.transliteration: Sumaatofon ga kyuusoku ni fukyuu shita.
example.translation: Smartphones spread rapidly.

example.term: 技術の発展が学びを変える。
example.transliteration: Gijutsu no hatten ga manabi o kaeru.
example.translation: Technological growth transforms learning.

example.term: 残された課題を整理する。
example.transliteration: Nokosareta kadai o seiri suru.
example.translation: Organize the remaining challenges.

example.term: 独学する人が増える傾向にある。
example.transliteration: Dokugaku suru hito ga fueru keikou ni aru.
example.translation: There is a trend toward self-study.

example.term: 科学的な根拠に基づく方法。
example.transliteration: Kagakuteki na konkyo ni motozuku houhou.
example.translation: A method grounded in scientific evidence.

lessons.title: Economy & Resources
lessons.objective: Understand economic concepts, demand, and sustainability.
lessons.grammarNote: Pay attention to paired opposites: 需要 (demand) vs. 供給 (supply), 増加 (increase) vs. 減少 (decrease).

example.term: 語学アプリの需要が高まっている。
example.transliteration: Gogaku apuri no juyou ga takamatte iru.
example.translation: Demand for language apps is rising.

example.term: ユーザーの負担を減らす設計。
example.transliteration: Yuuzaa no futan o herasu sekkei.
example.translation: A design that reduces user burden.

example.term: 限られた資源を有効活用する。
example.transliteration: Kagirareta shigen o yuukou katsuyou suru.
example.translation: Use limited resources effectively.

example.term: 海外からの訪問者が増加した。
example.transliteration: Kaigai kara no houmonsha ga zouka shita.
example.translation: Visitors from abroad increased.

example.term: オフラインでも安定して動作する。
example.transliteration: Ofurain demo antei shite dousa suru.
example.translation: Operates stably even offline.

lessons.title: Data & Communication
lessons.objective: Describe sharing, accuracy, and digital tools.
lessons.grammarNote: Combine nouns like 共有 (sharing) and 変換 (conversion) with する.

example.term: 知識を世界中で共有する。
example.transliteration: Chishiki o sekaijuu de kyouyuu suru.
example.translation: Share knowledge around the world.

example.term: 正確な翻訳を心がける。
example.transliteration: Seikaku na honyaku o kokorogakeru.
example.translation: Strive for accurate translation.

example.term: モジュール構成で管理しやすい。
example.transliteration: Mojuuru kousei de kanri shiyasui.
example.translation: Easy to manage with modular structure.

example.term: 多言語対応を標準装備した。
example.transliteration: Tagengo taiou o hyoujun soubi shita.
example.translation: Built in multi-language support as standard.

example.term: 空き時間を上手に活用しよう。
example.transliteration: Akijikan o jouzu ni katsuyou shiyou.
example.translation: Make smart use of spare time.

units.title: Formal Grammar & Essay Reading
units.subtitle: ろんせつとどっかい · Written conjunctions and abstract reasoning

lessons.title: Signature N2 Grammar
lessons.objective: Master contrast, parallel change, and conditional scope.
lessons.grammarNote: 〜にもかかわらず ('despite'), 〜に伴って ('along with'), 〜に応じて ('depending on').

example.term: 軽量にもかかわらず多機能だ。
example.transliteration: Keiryou ni mo kakawarazu takinou da.
example.translation: Despite being lightweight, it is feature-rich.

example.term: 進歩に伴って課題も変わる。
example.transliteration: Shinpo ni tomonatte kadai mo kawaru.
example.translation: Challenges change along with progress.

example.term: 実力に応じて飛び級できる。
example.transliteration: Jitsuryoku ni oujite tobikyuu dekiru.
example.translation: You can jump ahead according to your level.

example.term: 大きいから良いわけではない。
example.transliteration: Ookii kara yoi wake de wa nai.
example.translation: Just because it's big doesn't mean it's better.

items.translation: As long as / As far as

example.term: 私が知る限り問題はない。
example.transliteration: Watashi ga shiru kagiri mondai wa nai.
example.translation: As far as I know, there's no problem.

lessons.title: Written Conjunctions
lessons.objective: Follow logical flow across essays and long readings.
lessons.grammarNote: 一方 (on the other hand), したがって (therefore), すなわち (namely).

example.term: 便利な一方で注意点もある。
example.transliteration: Benri na ippou de chuuiten mo aru.
example.translation: While convenient, on the other hand there are caveats.

example.term: したがってバックアップが重要だ。
example.transliteration: Shitagatte bakkuappu ga juuyou da.
example.translation: Therefore, backups are important.

example.term: 継続、すなわち習慣化が鍵だ。
example.transliteration: Keizoku, sunawachi shuukanka ga kagi da.
example.translation: Continuity—namely habit-building—is key.

example.term: 複雑どころか、むしろ簡潔だ。
example.transliteration: Fukuzatsu dokoro ka, mushiro kanketsu da.
example.translation: Far from complex—rather, it is concise.

example.term: 長文の要点を短く要約した。
example.transliteration: Choubun no youten o mijikaku youyaku shita.
example.translation: Briefly summarized the long passage's key points.

lessons.title: Abstract Reasoning
lessons.grammarNote: N2 reading comprehension centers on author intent (主張), premise (前提), and perspective (視点).

example.term: 共通の前提から議論を始める。
example.transliteration: Kyoutsuu no zentei kara giron o hajimeru.
example.translation: Start the discussion from a shared premise.

example.term: 学習者の視点でUIを見直す。
example.transliteration: Gakushuusha no shiten de UI o minaosu.
example.translation: Revisit the UI from the learner's perspective.

example.term: 音声と反復は語学に不可欠だ。
example.transliteration: Onsei to hanpuku wa gogaku ni fukaketsu da.
example.translation: Audio and repetition are indispensable to language learning.

example.term: その説明には矛盾がない。
example.transliteration: Sono setsumei ni wa mujun ga nai.
example.translation: There is no contradiction in that explanation.

example.term: 文脈によって解釈が変わる。
example.transliteration: Bunmyaku ni yotte kaishaku ga kawaru.
example.translation: Interpretation changes with context.
